sections.h2: A Streamwood owner's options for selling
sections.html:
Three doors are open to a Streamwood seller: a broker's listing, a sale you manage alone, or a buyer who pays cash and takes the house untouched. Repairs, renters and the date you need funds usually settle the question.

  • Broker's listing: rewards a house in good order, provided you can sit through inspections and a lender's schedule.
  • Going alone: saves the commission and hands you the pricing, advertising and contract review.
  • Cash, untouched: no buyer repair demands, which suits a worn, inherited or tenant-occupied house.

Rented houses carry a Streamwood-specific wrinkle. The village licenses every rental property, single-family homes and condominium units included, so a landlord who sells should ask what happens to the license at transfer.

sections.h2: Streamwood prices and who lives here
sections.html:
Streamwood has an estimated 38,277 residents in 13,057 households averaging 2.97 people. Owners live in 89.0% of homes, the middle value is $271,200, and middle gross rent is $1,809. Owner cost per month runs $1,907 with a mortgage and $880 without one, and the middle household income is $101,218.

Inspectors for a buyer will focus on roofs, gutters and basements. Elgin Area School District U-46 serves most of the village, but boundaries split near Barrington Road and Route 59 for schools, libraries and park districts. Tell buyers which district, library and park district apply to your address. The nearest Metra station is in Bartlett, on the Milwaukee District West Line to Chicago Union Station.

Streamwood has its own real estate transfer stamp, issued by the Finance Department. Three items must reach the village before a stamp is issued:

  • A copy of the deed.
  • A copy of the state's Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration.
  • Payment of all outstanding water and sewer charges, including any assessments or penalties owed to the village.

Send completed forms to finance@streamwood.org, or call the Finance Department at (630) 736-3810. The closing attorney or title company normally files these, yet the water and sewer clearance is one the seller should expect. Pay those balances first, because the village will not issue the stamp until every charge is cleared.

A single-family or condo rental license costs $155 per building per year, includes the required inspection, and expires December 31. Landlords must finish a free online Crime Free Housing seminar of about an hour before applying. Each rental needs an interior and exterior inspection before the one-year license is issued, and the license must be renewed and paid for every year.

  • The tenant, or the landlord acting for the tenant, signs an inspection consent form before the village schedules the visit.
  • Landlords must show a certificate from the Crime Free Housing seminar. The village accepts one issued within the last five years by a community in Cook, DuPage, Kane, McHenry or Will County.
  • A sample Crime Free addendum for leases is posted on the village page.

Treat the license as part of the house's paperwork. A buyer who plans to keep the tenants should ask for the license record and the latest inspection result. A buyer who wants the house empty will want to know the lease end date before closing. A cash buyer can take a rented house, but the lease still has to be read first. Keep the license in force while the house is rented, and ask your attorney how a tenant's lease passes to the buyer.

sections.h2: Who assesses and bills Streamwood property taxes?
sections.html:
The village does not provide property tax services. Hanover Township handles assessment through the Cook County Assessor, and the Cook County Treasurer collects the tax. Ask the Treasurer about current bills at (312) 443-5100, and take past years or delinquent taxes to the Cook County Clerk at (312) 603-5645.

Cook County reassesses each property once every three years, on a township schedule, and north suburban townships such as Hanover are reassessed only where something about a property has changed. The last day to file an appeal with the Assessor for Hanover this cycle is December 7, 2026.

  • Look up your parcel number and notice on the Assessor's website.
  • Find out from the Assessor which exemptions are attached to your parcel.
  • Have your closing attorney explain how the year's bill is divided with the buyer.

sections.h2: What the Cook County deed needs
sections.html:
Deeds for Streamwood property are recorded by the Cook County Clerk. Its checklist includes the common address, the Property Index Number, a legal description, mail-to and prepared-by names, grantor and grantee details and a completed MyDec form for the state and county stamps. It also lists the municipality's real estate transfer tax, which is where the Streamwood stamp comes in.

For an exempt transfer, the deed needs exemption language citing 35 ILCS 200/31-45 and Cook County Ordinance 93-O-27, or a grantor and grantee affidavit. Section 31-15 of the Property Tax Code sets the state rate at 50 cents per $500 of value, and your title company can confirm the county amount.

sections.h2: A cash sale in Streamwood, start to finish
sections.html: A cash buyer skips showings, a lender's appraisal and the repair list, but the village steps still apply. Pay the water and sewer balance, send the deed and transfer declaration to Finance, and receive the stamp. Then the Cook County Clerk records the deed. If the house is a rental, have the license record and last inspection result ready for the buyer. Put the price, the closing date and the lease terms in writing before you sign. Ask the buyer to confirm who pays for the village stamp, since the contract decides it, and keep copies of the stamped deed and the closing statement for your own files once everything records. If a question arises, the Finance Department can usually answer it in one call.

sections.h2: Papers to gather before you list
sections.html: A short folder prevents delays. Collect your deed, the latest tax bill and the parcel number, the water and sewer account details, and receipts for roof or gutter work. For a rental, add the license, the latest inspection result, the lease and any Crime Free addendum. Give the closing attorney or title company a copy right away so the transfer declaration and the village stamp request can be prepared while you line up a buyer. If you live elsewhere, name one contact who can answer the village if a question comes up.

faqs.q: Does Streamwood charge its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The village's Finance Department prints a rate of $3.00 per $1,000 of value, and it issues the stamp after receiving the deed, the state transfer declaration and proof that water and sewer charges are paid.

faqs.q: Should a landlord keep the Streamwood rental license while selling?
faqs.a: Streamwood requires a license for every rental, at $155 per building per year with an inspection. Keep it in force while the house is rented, and ask your attorney how a tenant's lease passes to the buyer.

faqs.q: Which office assesses a Streamwood home?
faqs.a: Hanover Township does the local assessing through the Cook County Assessor, and the Cook County Treasurer collects the tax. The village itself does not handle assessments or bills.

faqs.q: What happens to water and sewer balances at closing?
faqs.a: Pay them first. The village will not issue the transfer stamp until all outstanding charges, assessments and penalties are cleared.

faqs.q: What does an exempt Streamwood transfer cost?
faqs.a: A transfer that changes the deed with no money exchanged needs a $10 exempt stamp. The application requires a signed, notarized deed.
